name: Marketing strategy to first-life program
description: One Marketing Room execution turns retained company evidence into one complete strategy and its executable first-life portfolio; deterministic materialization follows without another Room turn.

fields.description: Persisted company identity and onboarding context.
Persisted first-life baseline observations and evidence references.
The retained first-life operating instruction in the user's locale.

stages.objective: Create one polished go-to-market strategy and two to four useful first-life Runtime task proposals in a single Marketing Room run. Use retained onboarding, baseline, administrator status when present, company memory, and available evidence. Load relevant Marketing skills directly and synthesize once; do not run another planning or validation conversation. Clearly distinguish observed facts, reasonable professional recommendations, and material unknowns. Define a specific positioning wedge, best-fit audience, offer framing, messaging pillars, channel rationale, risks, and practical measures. Prefer a balanced portfolio containing a market-response campaign, localized pipeline or outreach preparation, and competitor or market-opportunity research when those motions fit the company, but choose only the strongest two to four tasks rather than padding or failing because one category lacks evidence. Recommendations may use strategy-artifact lineage when external sources are limited; never present a recommendation as an observed fact or invent guarantees. Avoid unsupported precision: use directional or checkpoint-based success measures unless a numeric target is directly supported. Each proposal states title, bounded objective, reason, expected outcome, practical success measure, available evidence references, dependencies, motion class, effect class, priority, and optional exact targets. Do not select a playbook, Company Room, provider, supported action, or execution mechanism. Perform no provider action.
Validate and materialize the accepted provider-neutral portfolio as ordered, idempotent proposed Runtime tasks.
